entries.name: Network performance
entries.definition: How fast, reliable and responsive a network is, judged by measures such as latency, throughput and packet loss.

entries.name: Network topology
entries.definition: The arrangement of the nodes and links in a network, such as bus, star, ring and mesh.

entries.name: Neural networks
entries.definition: Designing and reasoning about networks of learned computational units.

entries.name: Neurobiology
entries.definition: The branch of biology that studies the nervous system and how it develops and works.

entries.name: Neuromuscular medicine
entries.definition: The medical subspecialty that diagnoses and treats diseases of the nerves, the muscles and the junctions between them.

entries.name: Neuromuscular system and disorders
entries.definition: How the nerves and muscles work together and the diseases that disrupt them.

entries.name: Neurosurgery
entries.definition: The surgical specialty that treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves.

entries.name: Nexpose
entries.definition: Rapid7's vulnerability scanner, which finds and ranks security weaknesses in networks and systems.

entries.name: Next.js
entries.definition: A React-based framework for building server-rendered and static web applications.

entries.name: NFPA 70E
entries.definition: A National Fire Protection Association standard for electrical safety in the workplace in the United States.

entries.name: nice (Unix utility)
entries.definition: A Unix command that runs a program with a changed scheduling priority.

entries.name: NICE Workforce Management
entries.definition: Workforce management software from NICE for forecasting workload and scheduling staff in contact centres.

entries.name: Nightwatch.js
entries.definition: An end-to-end testing framework for web applications that runs on Node.js and drives browsers through WebDriver.

entries.name: NIH Stroke Scale
entries.definition: A standardised neurological examination scale that measures the severity of stroke symptoms.

entries.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
entries.definition: A voluntary framework from NIST that organises cybersecurity activities into functions such as identify, protect, detect, respond and recover.

entries.name: NIST SP 800-37
entries.definition: A NIST Special Publication that describes the Risk Management Framework for managing security and privacy risk in information systems.

entries.name: NIST SP 800-53
entries.definition: A NIST Special Publication that catalogues security and privacy controls for information systems and organisations.

entries.name: NIST SP 800 series
entries.definition: NIST's 800 series of Special Publications, which give guidelines and recommendations on information security.

entries.name: Nitrogen-phosphorus detector
entries.definition: A gas chromatography detector that responds selectively to compounds containing nitrogen or phosphorus.

entries.name: NLog
entries.definition: An open-source logging library for .NET applications.

entries.name: No Child Left Behind Act
entries.definition: A United States federal education law from the early 2000s that set testing and accountability requirements for public schools and was replaced in 2015 by the Every Student Succeeds Act.

entries.name: Node.js
entries.definition: A cross-platform JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that runs JavaScript outside the browser.

entries.name: Non-Facility Associated Signalling
entries.definition: An ISDN primary rate interface arrangement in which a single D channel carries the signalling for several PRI trunk groups.

entries.name: Non-fungible tokens
entries.definition: Unique blockchain-based tokens that record ownership of a digital or physical item.

entries.name: Nonverbal communication
entries.definition: Conveying and reading meaning without words, through body language, gestures, facial expression and tone.

entries.name: nosetests
entries.definition: The command-line test runner of nose, a Python unit testing framework that extends unittest.

entries.name: NoSQL database
entries.definition: A database that stores data in non-relational models such as documents, key-value pairs, columns or graphs.

entries.name: Notion (software)
entries.definition: A workspace app for notes, documents, wikis and databases.

entries.name: npm
entries.definition: The default package manager for Node.js, used to install and manage JavaScript packages.

entries.name: Nuance PDF Converter
entries.definition: Nuance software for creating, converting and editing PDF files.

entries.name: NumPy
entries.definition: A Python library for fast numerical computing built around N-dimensional arrays.

entries.name: NuoDB
entries.definition: A distributed SQL relational database designed to run in the cloud.

entries.name: Nutanix
entries.definition: A hyperconverged infrastructure platform that combines compute, storage and virtualisation on clustered servers.

entries.name: Nutanix AHV
entries.definition: Nutanix's built-in hypervisor, based on KVM, that runs virtual machines on Nutanix clusters.

entries.name: Nutanix Calm
entries.definition: Nutanix's application automation and orchestration tool for provisioning and managing applications across clouds.

entries.name: Nutanix Prism
entries.definition: Nutanix's web-based console for monitoring and managing Nutanix clusters.

entries.name: Nutraceuticals
entries.definition: Food-derived products, such as supplements and fortified foods, that are sold for health benefits beyond basic nutrition.

entries.name: Nutrition care planning
entries.definition: Writing individual plans that set a patient's nutrition goals, interventions and follow-up.

entries.name: Nutrition consulting
entries.definition: Advising individuals or organisations on diet and eating habits to meet health or performance goals.

entries.name: Nutrition diagnosis
entries.definition: The step of the Nutrition Care Process in which a dietitian identifies and names a nutrition problem that they are responsible for treating.
